extracted.intended_audience: state agency rulewriters, regulatory attorneys, local governments, small businesses, rural stakeholders, and other regulated parties interacting with New York State rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards in the New York Administrative Procedure Act governing preparation of regulatory impact statements, regulatory flexibility analyses, rural area flexibility analyses, regulatory agendas, guidance document publication, filing/effective-date rules, declaratory rulings, alternate implementation petitions, and related public-participation and compliance provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement — alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: (g) Alternative approaches. A statement indicating whether any significant alternatives to the rule were considered by the agency, including a discussion of such alternatives and the reasons why they were not incorporated into the rule;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the required regulatory impact statement; agency must discuss significant alternatives and explain why alternatives were not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement — federal standards
rubrics_metrics.description: (h) Federal standards. A statement identifying whether the rule exceeds any minimum standards of the federal government for the same or similar subject areas and, if so, an explanation of why the rule exceeds such standards;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must state if rule exceeds federal minimums and justify the reasons for exceeding federal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact statement — compliance schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Compliance schedule. A statement indicating the estimated period of time necessary to enable regulated persons to achieve compliance with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an estimated timeframe for regulated parties to come into compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated regulatory impact statements for related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce paperwork on the agencies, an agency may: (a) Consider a series of closely related and simultaneously proposed rules as one rule for the purpose of submitting a consolidated regulatory impact statement; and (b) Submit a consolidated regulatory impact statement for any series of virtually identical rules proposed in the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows agencies to consolidate impact statements for efficiency when rules are closely related or virtually identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption claim for technical amendment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may claim an exemption from the requirements of this section for a rule that involves only a technical amendment, provided, however, the agency shall state in the notice ... the reason or reasons for claiming such exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming exemption for technical amendments, agencies must explicitly state reasons in the notice of proposed rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for certain defined rules and consensus rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule defined in subparagraph (ii) of paragraph (a) of subdivision two of section one hundred two of this chapter shall be exempt ...; A rule determined by an agency to be a consensus rule and proposed pursuant to subparagraph (i) of paragraph (b) of subdivision one of section two hundred two of this article shall be exempt ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific categories (as defined elsewhere in statute) are exempt from regulatory impact statement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised regulatory impact statement — triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall issue a revised regulatory impact statement when: (a) the information presented ... is inadequate or incomplete ... (b) a proposed rule contains any substantial revisions ... (c) there are no substantial revisions ... but there are changes in the text of the rule as adopted ... and such changes would necessitate that such statement be modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions required when initial statement is inadequate, when substantive revisions occur, or when adoption-time textual changes affect the statement; long revisions (>2000 words) may be summarized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider minimizing adverse economic impact on small businesses/local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing a rule, the agency shall consider utilizing approaches that will accomplish the objectives of applicable statutes while minimizing any adverse economic impact of the rule on small businesses and local governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General duty to balance statutory objectives with minimizing economic harm to small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility — suggested approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with the objectives of applicable statutes, the agency shall consider such approaches as: (a) the establishment of differing compliance or reporting requirements or timetables that take into account the resources available to small businesses and local governments; (b) the use of performance rather than design standards; and (c) an exemption from coverage by the rule, or by any part thereof, for small businesses and local governments so long as the public health, safety or general welfare is not endangered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should evaluate flexible compliance schemes, performance-based standards, or exemptions for small entities when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility — cure period for penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing a rule for which a regulatory flexibility analysis is required and which involves the establishment or modification of a violation or of penalties associated with a violation, the agency shall: (a) include a cure period or other opportunity for ameliorative action ...; or (b) include in the regulatory flexibility analysis an explanation of why no such cure period was included in the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When new/modified penalties are involved, include a cure period or explain its absence in the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility analysis — required contents (small businesses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each regulatory flexibility analysis shall contain: (a) a description of the types and an estimate of the number of small businesses and local governments to which the rule will apply; (b) a description of (i) the reporting, recordkeeping and other compliance requirements of the rule, and (ii) the kinds of professional services that a small business or local government is likely to need in order to comply with such requirements; (c) an estimate of the initial capital costs and an estimate of the annual cost of complying ...; (d) an assessment of the economic and technological feasibility of compliance ...; (e) an indication of how the rule is designed to minimize any adverse economic impact ..., including information regarding whether the approaches suggested in subdivision one ... were considered; and (f) a statement indicating how the agency complied with subdivision six of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive analytic requirements covering affected entities, compliance burdens, cost estimates, feasibility, mitigation measures considered, and outreach compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility — exemptions and required finding
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) This section shall not apply to any rule defined ... nor shall it apply to any rule which does not impose an adverse economic impact ... The agency's finding and the reasons upon which the finding was made ... shall be included in the rule making notice ... (b) A rule determined by an agency to be a consensus rule ... shall be exempt ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an agency finds the rule does not impose adverse economic impacts, it must include the finding and reasons in the notice; some consensus/defined rules are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility — consolidation allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to avoid duplicative action, an agency may consider a series of closely related rules as one rule for the purpose of complying with subdivision two of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may treat related rules collectively to avoid duplication in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility — quantitative vs descriptive effects
rubrics_metrics.description: In complying with the provisions of subdivision two of this section, an agency may provide either a quantifiable or numerical description of the effects of a rule or more general descriptive statements if quantification is not practicable or reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows either numeric estimates or qualitative descriptions when quantification isn't practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility — outreach to small businesses/local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: When any rule is proposed for which a regulatory flexibility analysis is required, the agency shall assure that small businesses and local governments have been given an opportunity to participate ... through such activities as: (a) the publication of a general notice ...; (b) the direct notification of interested small businesses and local governments affected by the proposed rule; (c) the conduct of special open conferences concerning the proposed rule for small businesses and local governments affected by the rule; and (d) the adoption or modification of agency procedural rules to reduce the cost or complexity of participation ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must engage in targeted outreach activities to facilitate small-entity participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory flexibility — when to issue revised analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall issue a revised regulatory flexibility analysis when: (a) the information presented ... is inadequate or incomplete ..., (b) a proposed rule contains any substantial revisions ..., or (c) there are no substantial revisions ... but there are changes in the text of the rule as adopted ... and such changes would necessitate that such analysis be modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel to regulatory impact statement revision triggers; long revisions may be summarized if >2000 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural area flexibility analysis — intent and required consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing a rule, the agency shall consider utilizing approaches that will accomplish the objectives of applicable statutes while minimizing any adverse impact of the rule on public and private sector interests in rural areas ... consider such approaches as: (i) the establishment of differing compliance or reporting requirements or timetables ...; (ii) increased use of performance or outcome standards rather than design or input standards; and (iii) an exemption from coverage by the rule, or by any part thereof, so long as the public health, safety or general welfare is not endangered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to small-business flexibility but tailored to rural constraints (sparsity, limited services, reliance on volunteers); encourages flexible compliance and performance standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural area flexibility analysis — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rural area flexibility analysis shall contain: (a) A description of the types and an estimate of the number of rural areas to which the rule will apply; (b) A description of (i) the reporting, recordkeeping and other compliance requirements of the rule, and (ii) the kinds of professional services that are likely to be needed in a rural area ...; (c) An estimate of the initial capital costs and an estimate of the annual cost ...; (d) An indication of how the rule is designed to minimize any adverse impact of such rule on rural areas, including information regarding whether the approaches suggested in subdivision two ... were considered; and (e) A statement indicating how the agency complied with subdivision seven of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors small-business analysis but focused on rural impacts and services availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural area flexibility — outreach requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When any rule is proposed for which a rural area flexibility analysis is required, the agency shall assure that public and private interests in rural areas have been given an opportunity to participate ... through such activities as: (a) the publication of a general notice of the proposed rule making; (b) notification of public and private interests in rural areas directly affected by the proposed rule; (c) the conduct of special public hearings or meetings concerning the proposed rule for those public and private interests affected by the rule; and (d) the adoption or modification of agency procedural rules that will minimize the cost or complexity of participation in the rule making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted outreach modalities (publication, direct notice, hearings, procedural accommodations) to ensure rural participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural area flexibility — exemptions, consolidation, and revision triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: This section shall not apply to any rule defined ... nor shall it apply to any rule which does not impose an adverse impact on rural areas ... A rule determined by an agency to be a consensus rule ... shall be exempt ... In order to avoid duplicative action, an agency may consider a series of closely related rules as one rule ... When any rule is proposed for which a rural area flexibility analysis is required, each agency shall issue a revised rural area flexibility analysis when: (a) the information presented ... is inadequate or incomplete ...; (b) a proposed rule contains any substantial revisions ...; or (c) there are no substantial revisions ... but there are changes in the text of the rule as adopted ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel exemptions, consolidation options, and revision triggers as in the small-business analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agenda — contents and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulatory agenda shall be comprised of a list and brief description of subject matter being considered for rule making and the name, public office, address, e-mail address and telephone number of the agency representative ... Agencies shall publish the regulatory agendas and information related to such agendas on their respective websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agenda must identify subject matter and a knowledgeable agency contact; must be posted online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agenda — web updates and new listing notice
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may update the regulatory agenda on its website by adding a description of a rule ... Such description shall identify the date on which the description is first listed ... and shall conspicuously indicate that the description has been newly listed for a period of not less than thirty days after such date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Website updates permitted; new items must be flagged as newly listed for ≥30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agenda — identification of rules requiring flexibility analyses and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall identify each rule described in its regulatory agenda for which a regulatory flexibility analysis or a rural area flexibility analysis may be required, and shall provide outreach as appropriate to potentially affected small businesses, local governments and public and private interests in rural areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agenda must flag rules likely to require special analyses and plan outreach accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agenda — required summary content (≤2000 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulatory agenda shall be comprised of summaries of such rules. Each summary shall, in less than two thousand words, contain, in so far as practicable: (a) a description of the rule which the agency is considering; (b) a citation to the statutory authority ...; (c) a schedule of the dates for hearings, meetings or other opportunities for public participation ...; (d) the probable date on which the agency anticipates submitting ... a notice of proposed rule making ...; (e) the name, public office, address and telephone number of the agency representative ...; and (f) any other information which the agency determines will serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agencies submit agendas in January/May/September, each summary should include these elements and be concise (<2000 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance documents — annual public listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Not less than once each year, every agency shall submit to the secretary of state for publication in the state register a list of all guidance documents on which the agency currently relies, and provide information on where and how regulated parties and members of the public may inspect and obtain copies of any such document;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual requirement to publish what guidance documents agency relies on and how to obtain them (DEC exempted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance documents — website exemption and five-year review
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state may exempt an agency from compliance ... upon a determination that the agency has published on its website the full text of all guidance documents on which it currently relies ... Not less than once every five years, every agency shall conduct a process for reviewing and updating all guidance documents on which it currently relies. In conducting such process, the agency shall obtain feedback from regulated parties and members of the public who are directly or indirectly affected by the guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies publishing full text online may be exempted from register list; agencies must review guidance every five years and obtain affected-party feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and effective date — filing requirement and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in subdivision two of this section, no rule shall become effective until it is filed with the secretary of state and the notice of adoption is published in the state register ... unless: (i) a later date is required by statute or is specified in the rule, (ii) adopted as an emergency rule ..., or (iii) defined as a rule in subparagraph (ii) of paragraph (a) of subdivision two of section one hundred two of this chapter. Each rule submitted for filing shall have attached thereto the certificate required under subdivision two of section one hundred two of the executive law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules generally must be filed and published before taking effect, with enumerated exceptions and required certificate attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend/suspend/repeal prior to effective date — limits and filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may, after a rule is filed ... and prior to the effective date ... amend, suspend or repeal such rule prior to the effective date without complying with the provisions of subdivision one of section two hundred two of this article. ... An agency may not amend, suspend or repeal a rule pursuant to this subdivision if such action would constitute a substantial revision of the rule as adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies can change filed rules before they take effect but cannot do so if the change is a substantial revision; must file notice of adoption and compare texts for certain compliance purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of state rejection for expired notice period
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state shall reject any rule submitted for filing by an agency where the notice of proposed rule making for such rule has expired pursuant to the provisions of section two hundred two of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing will be rejected if the earlier notice of proposed rulemaking period has expired without compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model plans for required written plans/compliance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rule requires a regulated party to develop a written plan or compliance document ... the agency is required to, upon request of one or more regulated parties, prepare a model of such a written plan or compliance document to provide guidance as to the content and form ... The availability of any such model plan or document shall be communicated ... and shall be made available ... the agency may extend the final date for submitting a written plan ... for an additional period, not to exceed ninety days, if such an extension is deemed necessary to permit regulated parties to use the model plan as guidance ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must prepare and publish model plans on request, communicate availability, and may extend submission deadlines up to 90 days to allow use of model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory rulings — agency authority and form
rubrics_metrics.description: On petition of any person, an agency may issue a declaratory ruling with respect to (i) the applicability ... of any rule or statute enforceable by it, or (ii) whether any action by it should be taken pursuant to a rule. Each agency shall prescribe by rule the form for such petitions and the procedure for their submission, consideration and disposition. A declaratory ruling shall be binding upon the agency unless it is altered or set aside by a court. ... A declaratory ruling shall be made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must adopt petition form/procedure, rulings are binding (subject to court), public, and subject to Article 78 review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory rulings — timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Within thirty days of receipt of a petition ... an agency shall issue either a declaratory ruling or a statement declining to issue a declaratory ruling, unless the agency's rules provide for a different time period not to exceed sixty days ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default 30-day decision/decline deadline unless agency rule allows up to 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory rulings — court petitioning allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding any inconsistent provision of law, a person may submit a petition in the manner provided for in article seventy-eight ... without first applying for a declaratory ruling pursuant to paragraph (ii) of subdivision one of this section, or to the office for an advisory opinion pursuant to this subdivision. A person may concurrently petition the court ... and petition the agency ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners can go directly to court (Article 78) without first seeking agency declaratory ruling and may proceed concurrently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate methods petitions — required petition contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition shall include: (a) an indication that submission has been approved by the governing body ...; (b) an identification of the regulatory mandate ... and information sufficient to establish that the proposed alternate method ... is consistent with and will effectively carry out the objectives of the regulatory mandate; (c) information on the process used by the local government to ensure that all stakeholders have been appropriately involved ...; (d) documentation that the petition has been submitted to the authorized agents of any certified or recognized employee organizations ...; (e) a proposed plan and timetable for compiling and reporting information to facilitate evaluation of the effectiveness of the alternate method; (f) if the state provides financial assistance ... any proposed amount or percentage of such assistance which would be returned ...; and (g) the name, public office address and telephone number of the representative ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition content requirements are detailed and emphasize stakeholder involvement, evaluation plans, employee-organization notification, and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate methods — joint petitions and allocation of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more local governments may submit a petition jointly, provided that each local government meets the requirements of paragraphs (a), (c), (d) and (g) ... and provided that the petition addresses the manner in which responsibility for implementation will be allocated between or among the participating local governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint petitions allowed but each participating local government must meet specified requirements and petition must allocate implementation responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate methods — notice, comment period, and publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall cause a notice of the petition to be published in the state register and shall receive comments on the petition for a period of thirty days. Such notice shall either include the full text of the information set forth in the petition or shall set forth the address of a website on which the full text has been posted. The notice shall include the name, public office address and telephone number ... of an agency representative ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must publish notice, permit 30-day comments, and either include full petition text or post it online and provide agency contact info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate methods — agency decision standard and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Not later than thirty days after the last day of the comment period, the agency shall approve or disapprove the petition. ... The agency shall not grant a petition unless it determines that the petition has met the requirements of subdivision two of this section and that the local government has established that the alternate method is consistent with and will effectively carry out the objectives of the regulatory mandate; provided, however, that no petition shall be approved which would result in the contravention of any environmental, health or safety standard or would reduce any benefits or rights accorded by law or rule to third parties. In approving a petition, an agency may waive a statutory provision only if it is specifically authorized by law to waive such provision. An approval shall include a timetable for agency evaluation of the effectiveness of the alternate method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must decide within 30 days post-comment period, approve only if alternate method meets statutory objectives and does not contravene standards or reduce third-party rights; approval includes evaluation timetable and waivers only if authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate methods — employee-organization objections and hearing rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of an objection to a petition from the authorized agent of any certified or recognized employee organization ... the agency shall provide any such organizations with an opportunity for a hearing. If an adjudicatory proceeding is requested, the petition shall not be approved unless the agency determines by a preponderance of the evidence that implementing the alternate method would not affect such employees by contravening any environmental, health or safety standard, reducing any rights or benefits or violating the terms of any negotiated agreement ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employee organizations may trigger hearings; adjudicatory burden is preponderance of the evidence to show no adverse effect on employees' rights/benefits or standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate methods — agency evaluation, rescission, and incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the timetable established ... the agency shall evaluate the effectiveness of the alternate method ... The evaluation shall identify any savings or other benefits, and any costs or other disadvantages ... and shall address the desirability of incorporating the alternate method into the rules of the agency. Notice of availability of the evaluation shall be published in the state register. A state agency may rescind its approval of a petition at any time if it determines ... that the alternate method is not effectively carrying out the objectives ... or is being implemented in a manner detrimental to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires post-implementation evaluation, publication of evaluation, and authority to rescind approvals if alternate method fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review of rules — exhaustion/time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless an exclusive procedure or remedy is provided by law, judicial review of rules may be had upon petition presented under article seventy-eight ... The agency shall be made a party to the proceedings. Such a special proceeding ... may not be maintained unless the petitioner has first requested the agency to pass upon the validity or applicability of the rule in question and action has been taken upon such request or more than thirty days has elapsed since such request has been filed and no final action has been taken thereon or the agency has not provided for the issuance of such declaratory rulings under section two hundred four. Unless the agency acts upon such request within thirty days of its filing, such request shall be deemed to have been denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires petitioners to seek agency action first (with 30-day deemed-denial rule) before Article 78 unless an exclusive remedy exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping regulations — federal-state compliance petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person subject to a requirement imposed by a state statute or rule and to a similar requirement imposed by the federal government, may ... petition the agency ... for a declaratory ruling as to whether compliance with the federal requirement will be accepted as compliance with the state requirement. Upon receipt of such petition, the agency shall submit a copy thereof to the office of business permits and regulatory assistance. If the agency determines that compliance with the federal requirement would not satisfy the purposes or relevant provisions of the state statute involved, the agency shall so inform the petitioner in writing stating the reasons therefor and may issue a declaratory ruling to that effect. A copy of such written statement of reasons and any such declaratory ruling shall be submitted by the agency to the office of business permits and regulatory assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a process for seeking state acceptance of federal compliance; requires agency to notify both petitioner and office of business permits and to provide written reasons if denying equivalence.
